title: U.S. House · California's 12th Congressional District
area: The East Bay, including Oakland, Berkeley, Alameda, Albany, Emeryville, Piedmont, and San Leandro.

context.text: This district's boundaries changed under California Proposition 50, the mid-decade congressional redistricting measure voters approved in November 2025. Incumbent Lateefah Simon and fellow Democrat Jamie Joyce advanced from the June 2, 2026 top-two primary, defeating Stephen Slauson; because California uses a top-two primary in which all candidates run on one ballot, both Simon and Joyce are Democrats and will face each other in the general election.

candidates.name: Lateefah Simon
candidates.currentRole: U.S. Representative for California's 12th Congressional District (since 2025)

summary.text: Lateefah Simon is the Democratic incumbent representing California's 12th Congressional District in the East Bay, which she has held since January 2025. She began as a youth-justice advocate in her teens and later led civil-rights and philanthropic organizations, served on the BART Board of Directors from 2016 to 2024, and was elected to Congress in 2024. She is running for re-election.

background.text: Born in San Francisco, California, in 1977. Earned a bachelor's degree in public policy from Mills College in 2009 and a Master of Public Administration from the University of San Francisco in 2022.

According to her official biography, her career began in her late teens at the Young Women's Freedom Center, where she became executive director at 19, working with young women and girls in the criminal justice and foster care systems. She later led the Back on Track program, an alternative-to-incarceration initiative for first-time nonviolent offenders, in partnership with then-San Francisco District Attorney Kamala Harris.

Served as executive director of the Lawyers' Committee for Civil Rights of the San Francisco Bay Area, program director at the Rosenberg Foundation, and president of the Akonadi Foundation and the Meadow Fund, according to her official biography.
Appointed by then-Gov. Jerry Brown in 2016 to the Board of Trustees of the California State University; appointed by Gov. Gavin Newsom in 2020 as a senior advisor on police reform.

Elected to the Bay Area Rapid Transit (BART) Board of Directors in 2016 and served through 2024, including as Board President from 2020 to 2024; her office says she launched BART's Ambassador Program.

Elected to the U.S. House in November 2024, defeating fellow Democrat Jennifer Tran in the general election for the seat previously held by Barbara Lee; Ballotpedia lists her tenure as beginning in 2025.

Serves on the House Oversight and Government Reform Committee and the Small Business Committee in the 119th Congress. Her office says she is a Deputy Whip for Policy and a Vice Chair of the Congressional Progressive Caucus.

Her office lists recognitions including a MacArthur Fellowship, the John F. Kennedy Frontier Leadership Award, and the Jefferson Award for Public Service. She states that she is a mother of two daughters.

priorities.text: Campaign site lists priorities including affordable housing, homelessness, affordability and job creation, healthcare for all, and racial and social justice, describing a coalition of over 150 organizations built over three decades of advocacy.
Campaign site also lists reproductive freedom, immigration, LGBTQ+ rights, disability rights, and voting rights and democracy reform among her priorities.

positions.summary: Her campaign site says she will fight to expand and protect health coverage, advocating a public option and working toward a single-payer system.
positions.quote: advocating for a public option and ultimately working towards an affordable single-payer health system

positions.summary: Her campaign site says she will fight to guarantee access to safe and legal abortion.
positions.quote: will fight tirelessly to guarantee that every woman, no matter where she lives or how much she makes, has access to safe and legal abortion

positions.summary: Her campaign site says she will build on the Inflation Reduction Act and pass the Green New Deal, and describes a transition to net-zero emissions and clean energy investment.
positions.quote: Lateefah will stand up to the fossil fuel industry and work with colleagues to build on the progress made in the Inflation Reduction Act and pass the Green New Deal

record.text: Assigned to the House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform (Federal Law Enforcement Subcommittee; Health Care and Financial Services Subcommittee) and the House Committee on Small Business (Innovation, Entrepreneurship, and Workforce Development; Oversight, Investigations, and Regulations) in the 119th Congress (2025-2026).
Served on the Bay Area Rapid Transit (BART) Board of Directors after her 2016 election, and as a senior advisor on police reform to Gov. Gavin Newsom starting in 2020.

candidates.name: Jamie Joyce
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced from the June 2, 2026 top-two primary as the only challenger to Rep. Simon.

summary.text: Jamie Joyce is a Berkeley-based technologist, researcher, and nonprofit founder challenging incumbent Lateefah Simon in the general election; both are Democrats. According to her Ballotpedia profile, she founded the Society Library nonprofit and has worked on government-transparency projects at the Internet Archive. Her campaign centers on artificial-intelligence policy, government transparency, and a 650-page bill she has drafted, which she calls the MAD Act.

background.text: Born in New Hampshire and now living in Berkeley, according to Ballotpedia.

Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey describes her as a "multidisciplinary expert, executive, and researcher living in Berkeley" who has led AI teams and been interviewed for a documentary on artificial intelligence.

Before her work in technology, she says she oversaw environmental and humanitarian projects, working with vulnerable communities in more than 20 countries; Ballotpedia lists her as chief operating officer of the international organization IDEAS For Us.

Founded the Society Library nonprofit and co-founded the Canonical Debate Labs research group; Ballotpedia lists her as program co-lead of the Internet Archive's Democracy's Library program. She says she has spent nearly a decade building technology tools that help governments make policy decisions, including legislative drafting tools.

Has served in board and advisory roles at Wikitongues and Atlas Computing, and received a Collective Intelligence Fellowship from the Foresight Institute and an AI for Human Reasoning Fellowship from the Future of Life Foundation, according to Ballotpedia.
Advanced from the June 2, 2026 top-two primary, where she received 15.6% of the vote to Simon's 84.2%.

priorities.text: Says she has drafted a 650-page bill she calls the MAD Act, which would strengthen dark-money disclosure requirements, place hard limits on surveillance, set guardrails on AI, and create accountability related to the Epstein network.
priorities.quote: I wrote the MAD Act, 650 pages of real legislation, drafted and ready. It puts teeth on dark money disclosure, hard limits on surveillance, guardrails on AI, and real accountability for the Epstein network.

priorities.text: Says she is working to build a bloc of 11 or more members of Congress who would withhold votes from legislation that does not serve voters first.
Says she respects Rep. Simon's civil-rights and oversight work but believes the moment requires affirmative AI legislation and aggressive executive-branch oversight rather than incremental progress.
priorities.quote: Jamie respects Rep. Simon's civil rights and oversight work, but this moment requires affirmative AI legislation and aggressive action to keep the executive branch in check.

candidates.researchNotes: Campaign website (jamiejoyce.com) and a blog post on Gaza found Oct. 2026; her platform centers on the MAD Act (AI, surveillance, ICE, dark money, election reform, Epstein files). Her pages do not squarely state a side on the tracked issues, so only statements are recorded.

statements.quote: This bill pulls untrained ICE and CBP officers off our streets immediately while leaving officers who have been stationed in communities for years and who have clean records to continue their work dealing with human trafficking and truly criminal cases.
statements.context: On a fact sheet for her MAD Act (Title VIII), which her campaign site links as her bill

statements.quote: Especially when their debt-to-GDP ratio suggests they can afford to maintain their own Iron Dome.
statements.context: In a May 28, 2026 post on her campaign blog about pro-Israel PAC money
